name: travel-advice-world-map
what_it_holds: Interactive world map of Australian Government (Smartraveller) travel advice levels and visa requirements for Australian passport holders. Updated 2026-09-13 (unofficial project pulling the Smartraveller source).
why_useful: A third sovereign advisory source (Australia) -- useful for APAC-outbound demand-shock cross-checks and diversifying single-country advisory risk; also carries visa-requirement data, a separate friction variable on cross-border travel not covered by any of our current holdings.
geography: global via Australian Smartraveller, APAC-outbound angle
themes: Insurance, safety and travel advisories datasets (State Dept advisories history, travel insurance claims, crime by city) as demand shocks
why_all: A third sovereign advisory source (Australia) -- useful for APAC-outbound demand-shock cross-checks and diversifying single-country advisory risk; also carries visa-requirement data, a separate friction variable on cross-border travel not covered by any of our current holdings.

name: api-evangelist/predicthq
what_it_holds: Third-party API profile (OpenAPI spec, Postman/Open Collection files) of the PredictHQ Events API, a commercial demand-intelligence platform covering conferences, concerts, sports, community events, public holidays, school terms and severe weather across many countries with predicted-attendance/rank features. No data committed here — it documents how to call the live API (requires a PredictHQ account/API key, free tier exists with limited calls). Companion repo pipeworx-io/mcp-predicthq wraps the same API as an MCP tool.
why_useful: PredictHQ's conference/MICE + event-impact category is the closest machine-pullable proxy we found for CONTEXT.md gap #11 (events/shocks calendar with predicted demand impact, could time FIFA World Cup 2026, major conferences, concerts against nights/ADR spikes by market).
time_coverage: Live/forward-looking; historical event archive depth depends on PredictHQ plan
license: N/A (documentation repo is public; underlying API is commercial/freemium)
themes: Corporate travel and business-travel data (GBTA, Concur/SAP, Navan public indices, conference calendars), MICE datasets
why_all: PredictHQ's conference/MICE + event-impact category is the closest machine-pullable proxy we found for CONTEXT.md gap #11 (events/shocks calendar with predicted demand impact, could time FIFA World Cup 2026, major conferences, concerts against nights/ADR spikes by market).

name: scholar-8/10times
what_it_holds: Python scraper (src/ modules for parsing, date extraction, JSON export) targeting 10times.com's Top-100 conference/trade-show rankings across 30+ industry categories worldwide. No committed dataset — output format shown only as an example JSON record (event name, dates, location, rating, URL). Presented as a portfolio/demo piece by a scraping shop (Bitbash), not a maintained data product.
why_useful: 10times.com is the largest public conference/trade-show/MICE calendar (thousands of B2B events, dates, cities, expected attendance where published); a working scraper pattern would let us build our own conference-density-by-city series for MICE-driven business travel demand, feeding gap #11. Scraping a non-Airbnb site is in-scope per the repo rules (still requires a human ToS call before running).
time_coverage: Live/current listings only; no historical archive built in
size_hint: Small scraper repo, no data files

name: balaton-bshi (Balaton Satellite Health Index)
what_it_holds: Satellite-based algal-bloom + tourism monitoring system for Lake Balaton, Hungary: 14 lakeside settlements, 3km coastal buffers, 2018-2025 with 2026 projection. Explicitly uses NOAA VIIRS nighttime lights (~500m, monthly) as a 'tourism activity proxy' alongside Sentinel-2 NDCI (algal bloom) and MODIS LST. Output is a JSON file (balaton.json) plus GeoJSON zone definitions powering a bilingual dashboard; intermediate Parquet files not version-controlled.
why_useful: A working, recent (2026) real-world example of exactly this theme's method — VIIRS nightlights as a tourism-activity proxy at settlement level combined with environmental satellite data — directly reusable as a template/validation case for constructing an analogous nightlights-tourism proxy for Airbnb markets, even though the geography (Hungarian lake resort towns) is outside our current 13/123-market panel.
themes: Occupancy/demand estimation from satellite, nightlights, or imagery; parking-lot counts; Sentinel-based tourism activity
why_all: A working, recent (2026) real-world example of exactly this theme's method — VIIRS nightlights as a tourism-activity proxy at settlement level combined with environmental satellite data — directly reusable as a template/validation case for constructing an analogous nightlights-tourism proxy for Airbnb markets, even though the geography (Hungarian lake resort towns) is outside our current 13/123-market panel.

name: 2017-wmata-ridership-data
what_it_holds: Committed CSVs of Washington Metro (WMATA) intraday, station-level entrance/exit counts by four daily time segments (AM peak, midday, PM peak, evening) for three one-off mega-events: 2009 Obama inauguration, 2017 Trump inauguration, 2017 Women's March; raw OCR'd tables plus a cleaned, deduplicated combined dataset and a system-wide totals sheet.
why_useful: A worked example (methodology, not ABNB-relevant data itself) of turning transit ridership spikes into an event-attendance/visitor proxy — directly applicable as a template for building a FIFA World Cup 2026 host-city transit-surge indicator (gap #11) from MTA/other agencies' turnstile data around June-July 2026.
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: A worked example (methodology, not ABNB-relevant data itself) of turning transit ridership spikes into an event-attendance/visitor proxy — directly applicable as a template for building a FIFA World Cup 2026 host-city transit-surge indicator (gap #11) from MTA/other agencies' turnstile data around June-July 2026.
